obscure.chinese: 模糊的；晦澀的；鮮為人知的；遮蔽

exampleSentences.en: Steam began to obscure the bathroom mirror.
exampleSentences.zh: 水蒸氣開始遮住浴室鏡面。

exampleSentences.en: Technical jargon can obscure the assumptions underlying an economic model.
exampleSentences.zh: 技術術語可能掩蓋經濟模型背後的假設。

obscure.mnemonicHint: ob- 有『朝向、覆在上面』的感覺，scure 可聯想被遮暗；像霧覆上玻璃，使東西看不清，也延伸成文字晦澀或事物鮮為人知。

offensive.chinese: 冒犯的；令人不快的；攻擊性的

exampleSentences.en: That crude joke was offensive to several guests at dinner.
exampleSentences.zh: 那個低俗笑話冒犯了晚餐會上的幾位客人。

exampleSentences.en: The survey found that offensive advertising can damage consumers' trust in a brand.
exampleSentences.zh: 該調查發現，冒犯性的廣告可能損害消費者對品牌的信任。

offensive.mnemonicHint: offend 是「冒犯」，加形容詞字尾 -ive 成為 offensive；也可聯想球賽的 offense 是主動進攻，因此既有「攻擊性的」也有「冒犯的」意思。

exampleSentences.en: My older brother taught me how to ride a bicycle.
exampleSentences.zh: 我哥哥教我騎腳踏車。

exampleSentences.en: The study found that older adults benefited most from regular exercise.
exampleSentences.zh: 研究發現，年長者從規律運動中獲益最多。

exampleSentences.en: Dark clouds gathered in an ominous sky before the storm.
exampleSentences.zh: 暴風雨前烏雲在不祥的天空聚集。

exampleSentences.en: The ominous decline in biodiversity signals ecosystem collapse.
exampleSentences.zh: 生物多樣性的不祥下降預示生態系統崩潰。

ominous.mnemonicHint: omin(omen) + ous → 有不好預兆 → 不祥的

exampleSentences.en: The cat jumped onto the sofa beside me.
exampleSentences.zh: 那隻貓跳到我身旁的沙發上。

exampleSentences.en: The enzyme transfers a phosphate group onto the target protein.
exampleSentences.zh: 該酵素將磷酸基團轉移到目標蛋白質上。

onto.mnemonicHint: on 加 to，動作移到表面上

exampleSentences.en: Maya openly challenges the rule whenever it seems unfair.
exampleSentences.zh: 每當規則顯得不公平時，瑪雅就會公開質疑它。

exampleSentences.en: This finding openly challenges the assumption that economic growth always reduces inequality.
exampleSentences.zh: 這項發現公開挑戰了經濟成長必然降低不平等的假設。

openly challenges.mnemonicHint: openly 是「公開地」，challenges 是 challenge 遇到第三人稱單數主詞的形式；合起來就是某人不躲藏地把質疑擺上檯面。

opposable.chinese: 可反對的；可對置的（尤指拇指能與其他手指相對）

exampleSentences.en: An opposable thumb lets you grip a slippery jar securely.
exampleSentences.zh: 可與其他手指相對的拇指讓你能牢牢抓住濕滑的罐子。

exampleSentences.en: Primates use opposable digits to manipulate objects with remarkable precision.
exampleSentences.zh: 靈長類利用可對置的指頭，以驚人的精準度操控物體。

opposable.mnemonicHint: oppose（使相對、反對）加 -able（能夠）就是「能夠相對或被反對的」；想像拇指轉過來與食指面對面夾住硬幣。

exampleSentences.en: I placed an order for two sandwiches.
exampleSentences.zh: 我點了兩份三明治。

exampleSentences.en: The variables were entered into the model in a fixed order.
exampleSentences.zh: 各變項依固定順序輸入模型。

order.mnemonicHint: order 把事物排整齊，也可指下令或訂購。

outcast.chinese: 被排斥者；遭放逐的人；被排斥的

exampleSentences.en: After exposing the lie, Leo felt like an outcast among his former friends.
exampleSentences.zh: 揭穿謊言後，里歐覺得自己在昔日朋友之間像個被排斥的人。

exampleSentences.en: The novel portrays its protagonist as a social outcast who questions established customs.
exampleSentences.zh: 這部小說將主角描寫成一名質疑既定習俗的社會邊緣人。

outcast.mnemonicHint: out（出去）加 cast（丟、投）就是「被丟到群體外面的人」；把一個人從圈內 cast out，便成了 outcast。

outrageous.chinese: 令人憤慨的；駭人聽聞的；極端離譜的

exampleSentences.en: Charging fifty dollars for tap water is outrageous.
exampleSentences.zh: 一杯自來水收五十美元實在太離譜了。

exampleSentences.en: Critics condemned the outrageous misuse of public funds during the reconstruction project.
exampleSentences.zh: 批評者譴責重建計畫期間駭人聽聞的公款濫用行為。

outrageous.mnemonicHint: outrage 是強烈憤怒，加 -ous 變成「會引發強烈憤怒的」；價格或行為誇張到讓人喊出 outrage，就是 outrageous。

exampleSentences.en: The overwhelming majority voted in favor of the proposal.
exampleSentences.zh: 壓倒性多數投票贊成該提案。

exampleSentences.en: Students reported overwhelming stress during final exams.
exampleSentences.zh: 學生在期末考試期間報告了壓倒性的壓力。

overwhelming.mnemonicHint: over + whelm(submerge) + ing → 被淹沒的 → 壓倒性的
